correctness.rationale: Every active spectral mask occurs on an open set of DCT coefficient space; the continuous piecewise-affine map has global seminorm Lipschitz constant equal to maximum mask projection seminorm. Step decomposition h=h_0*1+sum differences*H_a reduces the seminorm to single-step images. The product of DCT step coefficient and its first difference is (2/n) sin(pi*k*a/n) sin(pi*k*b/n), exactly the DST-I projection kernel. Orthogonality yields the sqrt(n-1) column bound. Independent fair-mask signs and the fourth-moment inequality E|X|>=sqrt(E X²)/sqrt(3), together with the sine squared-product sum >=n/4, establish the explicit lower bound. Local open-cell pairs attain the maximum. Independent exhaustive masks n=2..8 and DST orthogonality tests passed; finite checks are not a substitute for the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The exact nonlinear two-input DCT-II BV coefficient is mathematically equivalent to the unconditional DST-I spectral-mask column-norm problem. Full Strang DCT analysis supplies the transform but not nonlinear shrinkage in path variation; Durand–Froment wavelet-TV reconstruction concerns another transform and optimization. The indexed prior Haar/Walsh BV thresholds have different bases and growth rates; no exact DCT-II law or dominating bound was identified. A general unconditional basis theorem could cover the Theta(sqrt n) rate and is a material residual priority caveat.
residual_risks: Classical unconditional trigonometric-basis estimates or more general projection theorems may imply some rate bounds; a complete survey was not available.
The optimal leading constant of L_n/sqrt(n) remains unknown and is not asserted.

value.rationale: The operator is Euclidean nonexpansive but amplifies the natural ordered signal graph variation by Theta(sqrt n). A sharp *attained* finite mask formula and all-dimensional rate characterize a substantive stability boundary for classical coefficient denoisers; this is more than a computational toy or generic norm equivalence.

final_claim: For real orthonormal DCT-II soft-thresholding of all nonconstant coefficients at lambda>0, the attained two-input path-variation Lipschitz coefficient is max over DST-I spectral masks of the largest absolute column sum, independent of lambda; 1/2+(n-2)/(2 sqrt(3n))<=L_n<=sqrt(n-1), so L_n=Theta(sqrt(n)), n>=2.
limitations: Real orthonormal DCT-II, positive scalar threshold, finite unweighted nonperiodic path total variation only.
Independent exact masks n<=8 are bounded diagnostics; the universal rate follows analytically.
